To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a four node LPTN can accurately model the thermal behavior of automotive traction PMSMs and that a combination of empirical identification and global optimisation can be used to identify the parameters of the LPTN.

a lumped parameter network for permanent magnet machines is designed with a focus on physical plausibility and that a particle swarm optimization is used to identify the model parameters based on comprehensive experimental data and physically motivated constraints.
a LPTN for a PMSM is designed, the LPTN parameter identification is performed based on experimental training data and the model accuracy is cross validated with independent load profiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a physically motivated LPTN for PMSMs and the development of an efficient empirical approach for the identification of the network parameters.
the design, empirical identification and validation of a physically motivated LPTN to monitor the thermal behaviour of PMSMs.
the design and empirical parameter identification of an accurate and reliable LPTN for automotive PMSMs, which can be used for monitoring critical temperatures in real time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides a new methodological approach for the identification of LPTNs of PMSM with physically motivated constraints, which can be applied to a broad range of different PMSMs.
the presented LPTN approach is able to accurately model the thermal behaviour of PMSM with physically motivated constraints.
the LPTN is able to accurately predict the motor temperatures in the considered operating range, which is a prerequisite for the application in a closed loop temperature controller.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a LPTN for a PMSM can be identified using a global search method and a comprehensive set of experimental training data.
we were able to develop a LPTN model that is able to accurately describe the temperature behaviour of a 60kW PMSM for a broad range of load profiles.

the proposed approach can be used to accurately estimate the temperatures of the PMSM under consideration and that it provides a basis for further investigations on the influence of temperature dependent parameters on the motor performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed LPTN can predict critical temperatures of the PMSM with sufficient accuracy and is thus a valuable tool for thermal management.
the proposed LPTN model is able to predict the motor temperature distribution with high accuracy for various load profiles, which can be used for monitoring and thermal control of PMSMs.
an LPTN model with only four nodes is able to capture the thermal behaviour of a 60kW PMSM with a high accuracy.
